purpose: Request first-party clarification of the current authoritative compressed distribution and dataset-file reuse terms without inferring rights from public-availability statements.

questions.text: What is the current authoritative location or access route for the compressed Gaze-in-the-Wild distribution used with the published processing code, including ProcessData and LabelData?
If a current archive or replacement copy is available, is it the original compressed public distribution or a canonical replacement, and how can exact-copy identity be verified?
What terms explicitly govern analysis/research use of the dataset files themselves, separate from the article licence and processing-code licence?
May the dataset files themselves be redistributed, mirrored, or bundled with research software, and under what exact terms or restrictions?
May derived metrics, trained-model outputs, validation reports, and non-reconstructive aggregate results be published if dataset-file redistribution is restricted?
Who currently has authority to confirm or grant these dataset-file reuse and redistribution terms?
If available, what authoritative metadata defines participant identities and the complete TrIdx-to-task mapping in the compressed distribution?
If available, what authoritative metadata defines distributed-file coordinate units/semantics and sampling cadence?
If available, are independently created labeller streams separately recoverable for the same gaze samples, and how are those streams identified in the authoritative distribution?
